questions.q: What are the five pillars of Seligman's PERMA model?
a: Positive emotion, engagement, relationships, meaning and accomplishment
Purpose, energy, resilience, mindfulness and achievement
Pleasure, exercise, rest, money and affection
Positivity, empathy, resolve, mastery and autonomy
questions.why: Lesson 1 builds the model from those five elements of a fulfilling life.

questions.q: How does the what went well exercise work?
a: Each night you write three good things and explain why they happened
You list five goals for tomorrow before going to sleep
You recall one happy childhood memory every morning
You tell a friend about a success once a week
questions.why: Lesson 2 says ten minutes a night for a week shows that your choices matter.

questions.q: Why does Seligman consider IQ a poor predictor of success?
a: It mainly measures thinking speed, only one of four contributing factors
It changes so much over a lifetime that it cannot be trusted
It rewards effort rather than natural ability
It predicts happiness better than it predicts achievement
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists planning, learning rate and effort alongside speed of thought.

questions.q: Which four things determine accomplishment, according to the summary?
a: Thinking speed, planning and revising, learning rate and effort
Talent, luck, connections and timing
Confidence, focus, discipline and optimism
Education, income, health and social status
questions.why: Lesson 3 says most of these can be learned, unlike a fixed IQ score.

questions.q: What does the kindness exercise ask you to do?
a: Do something nice for someone without expecting anything back
Compliment three strangers every morning before work
Donate a fixed share of your income each month
Volunteer for a charity at least once a week
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to notice how the unreturned gesture affects your own mood.
